title: Cleft lip and palate surgery
what: The surgeon joins the tissues of the lip or palate to close the cleft. Several surgeries at different ages are often needed.
why: When a child is born with a cleft lip or palate: for the appearance of the face, normal feeding, speech, and hearing.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours, with a few days in hospital
tell_doctor: How your child feeds and gains weight
A cold, cough, or fever in the past 2 weeks
Any problems with anesthesia in the family

prepare.title: Age
prepare.text: The lip is usually repaired in the first months of life, the palate most often before 1 to 1.5 years. Your surgeon will set the timing.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, a pediatrician checkup, and sometimes other doctors. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: The clinic sets strict times for no food, formula, and milk.

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Ask in advance how to feed your child after surgery: with a spoon, a syringe, or a special bottle.

bring: The bottle or feeding device you were told to bring
steps: Your child changes and is prepared for anesthesia
In the operating room, your child falls asleep
The surgeon joins the tissues of the lip or palate
Your child wakes up, and you are called in
Sometimes soft arm splints are put on so your child does not touch the stitches
feel: After surgery, your child is in pain. You will get children's painkillers
Swelling of the lip or face for a few days
Your child may be fussy and eat less at first
after: Feed on the doctor's plan, with soft or liquid food
Keep the stitches clean, as the nurse shows you
No pacifiers or hard toys in the mouth until allowed
Follow-up with the surgeon, a speech therapist, an ENT doctor, and an orthodontist
red_flags: Your child is not drinking and has few wet diapers
Bleeding from the mouth or the stitches
Trouble breathing or blue lips: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or the stitches have opened

faq.a: A thin scar usually remains, and it fades over time. Sometimes a later touch-up is done.
Most often yes, especially with timely surgery and a speech therapist.

reminders.text: Your child's surgery is tomorrow. Food and milk strictly until the time the clinic gave you. Bring the feeding device.
